Params: Static fills the open channel, mixed with the distant thunder of pirate guns and crashing waves.
I am the commanding officer of this fleet. State your purpose, soldier.
Thank you for holding your fire.
As the highest-ranking officer of the Gray fleet, I ask you to take in all of our surviving personnel.
But let me remind you—this is a war.
Why do you believe I would agree?
Because you didn't attack when the pirates arrived.
Because you understood the flag and the signal.
And that's enough for you to gamble on?
A bold judgment. You were the one who raised that flag first, soldier. It was a dangerous move.
You could've ended the battle while we were distracted.
Perhaps I'm only waiting for a better moment.
I wasn't betting on the moment. I was betting on you.
The fact that we're having this conversation means I won the bet, doesn't it?
This isn't about winning or losing.
I can hold my fire out of respect for your judgment, but I won't place my own soldiers at greater risk simply because I admire you.
"I give so that you may give."
If you agree, we'll hand over all of our remaining ammunition and supplies.
As you can see, our flagship has been badly damaged. It won't stay afloat much longer.
Why do you believe that's enough to persuade me?
After the battle we've fought, your ammunition reserves can't be in good shape either.
Once our fleet goes down, the pirates will turn on you.
Or I can spend the last of our ammunition fighting you instead.
Perhaps too much. Is this a request, or a threat?
I'll accept. But you understand what it means to hand your soldiers and supplies over to me.
The voice over the channel remains calm. There is no pleading and no attempt to soften the reality of the decision.
Adelyde taps one finger lightly against the table, her respect for the student growing.
Even in this position, they remain composed and dignified.
The student has already accounted for Red's dwindling ammunition. That also confirms that the long war of attrition was part of their plan from the beginning.
Without the pirates entering the battle, this student might truly have found a path to a draw within that 0.42 percent chance.
Handing over the ammunition is more than a gesture of good faith. It gives Red enough firepower to resist the pirates.
The student is making sure their soldiers will survive the pirates' attacks.
This isn't surrender in spirit. They're still fighting to the very end—to keep their people alive.
Amid the dark sea and a hopeless situation, the student's predicament and choice bring Adelyde back to a day she can never forget.
A bottomless black sea. Hellish flames. Wave after wave of wounded soldiers.
She plunged into the Styx to save them, but she couldn't reach everyone. Some voices and faces never rose above the water again.
She received honors for what she did.

But the helplessness of that day never released its grip. She wanted to save more people—everyone she could reach. By the end, she was soaked through and could no longer tell seawater from sweat or blood.
Report your remaining personnel and your reserves of ammunition, fuel, and fresh water.
The voice calmly provides each figure in exact detail.
First officer, report the remaining carrying capacity of every ship.
The first officer immediately gives her the numbers.
Send rescue vessels to the Gray flagship.
Bring the flagship alongside as well. Extend the boarding bridge and get their people across as quickly as possible.
During a brief lull in the pirate bombardment, Red's rescue vessel crosses the water and pulls alongside the Gray flagship's port side.
The boarding bridge drops into place, and its clamps lock onto the deck with a heavy thud.
The first group of wounded soldiers appears.
Some support each other. Some are carried on stretchers. Others drag themselves forward with one hand on the railing. One by one, Gray's soldiers cross the bridge and board Red's rescue vessel.
Adelyde watches the evacuation from the bridge.
There is no panic and no fighting for position. The soldiers leave in an orderly sequence based on the severity of their injuries. Whoever planned the evacuation considered every detail.
The first group clears the bridge. The second begins crossing.
The pirate guns haven't stopped. A galleon continues to close the distance, its shells striking the sea and throwing columns of water high into the air.
Ma'am, the pirates are closing in! Our right flank is taking fire!
Escort squadron, move toward the pirates and provide cover fire. Keep the evacuation bridge open.
The escort ships spread out and force the pirates' main line of fire back, giving the evacuation bridge a brief window of safety.
The third group of wounded begins crossing.
Adelyde keeps her eyes on the Gray flagship, studying every person who crosses the bridge.
Ma'am, the enemy evacuation is complete. According to the count—
She frowns. That can't be right. She watched every person cross, and none of them carried themselves like the commandant she had faced.
She doesn't know what the student truly looks like, but she's certain she'll recognize them the moment they stand before her.
She doesn't wait for the first officer to finish. She's already heading toward the boarding bridge.
On the deck of the Gray flagship...

Flames climb from the base of the mast, nearly reaching the old alliance flag above. The broken foremast hangs over the side, pinning part of the shattered railing beneath it. The flagship is barely holding together, and every widening crack warns that it won't last much longer.
Adelyde crosses the boarding bridge and steps onto the Gray flagship. The smell of oil and smoke hits her immediately.
She moves around the fallen rigging and passes through a hatch, only to come face-to-face with someone climbing up from below.
You're covered in soot and oil, your hair disheveled, with a stack of crumpled papers still in one hand.
You wear the system's anonymous default appearance, with no identifying features.
But Adelyde knows immediately that you're the person she's been fighting all along.
Fewer than ten steps separate you.
For the first time, Adelyde hears your voice without the static of the communications channel. It's exactly as she remembers—calm and steady.
Below deck. Checking the final headcount.
You stayed behind to make sure every last soldier had crossed safely.
You truly care about the same thing she does.
Adelyde wants to tell you that she understands and respects your principles, but she doesn't know how to begin.
After a brief hesitation, she says something else instead.
Your tactics were remarkably mature. You held your ground despite being outnumbered.
Is that a compliment? Thank you.
The decision to concede so you could save your people was just as unusual. Most others wouldn't make that call.
It's not a choice most people respect.
She looks at you, and her voice unexpectedly softens.
Another pirate volley lands nearby, making the deck tremble beneath your feet.
As the enemy commander, you should know that boarding this ship now wasn't a sensible decision.
But I'm willing to trust someone who puts lives first.
She pauses, then finally asks the question that brought her here.
As long as my soldiers are safe, that's enough.
My responsibility is to minimize the sacrifice and preserve a chance for this place to live on.
We didn't come onto this deck to kill.
War isn't the purpose. Life is.
The guns and waves continue to roar, but none of your words are lost beneath the noise.
It should be a belief engraved into every soldier's soul, yet few can still live by it when the situation becomes this desperate.
Yet every generation produces a few people who hold onto that conviction, and they are the reason human civilization continues to shine through every catastrophe.
Adelyde sees that light in this generation—in the student standing before her.
Adelyde was ridiculed time and again for holding onto such old-fashioned heroism.
Then, someone who seemed almost like an imaginary friend stood beside her as a child and anchored that belief deep within her. It remained with her throughout the years that followed.
Now, someone stands before her and takes up the same torch that has burned since the dawn of civilization.
I admire your convictions and your determination to save lives.
But you don't have to die for them.
If you understand how precious life is, then you should value your own as well.
You look past the deck toward the pirate galleons.
Red is struggling to hold them back. The pirates' firepower is not to be underestimated—even with both fleets' remaining resources, defeating them would come at a devastating cost.
Unless something can hit them hard enough to cripple their forces.
Something like a flagship ramming straight into their formation.
Adelyde understands. Her brow furrows, her tone hardening.
As a student, dying inside a tactical simulation can damage your consciousness. I've already agreed to save your people. You don't need to end this by sacrificing yourself.
There is something strangely familiar in you, but she dismisses it as deja vu.
I suspected it from the beginning, and the feeling only grew stronger. When you said you respected my decision—
You still haven't answered my question.
Instead of answering, you hold out the stack of papers. Adelyde takes it, confused.
They aren't charts or deployment plans. They're crew rosters.
The pages are covered in careful notes. Some names are circled—the missing and the dead. Far more have been checked off in firm, orderly strokes.
Every checked name belongs to someone who crossed the boarding bridge.
They need to live. As long as they're alive, there's still hope.
I'm glad you approve of my choice. Maybe we'll meet at F.O.S. someday.
A pirate shell strikes the far side of the deck. The explosion erupts around you, and the entire ship lurches violently.
Adelyde instinctively pulls you close to shield you, only to realize you're doing the same for her. You both move at almost the exact same moment, each trying to protect the other.
Adelyde turns to block the flying splinters, while you shield her from the shower of sparks with your back.
Your uneven breaths mingle. Adelyde feels heat and cold at once—the heat of the explosion, or perhaps your body against hers, and the cold wind carrying the promise of rain. The rain is coming.
In that moment, you become both shelter and anchor for each other.
The worst of the shaking passes, but you both know the ship's sinking is only a matter of time.
Adelyde grabs your wrist first, gripping it with all her strength.
Strangely, even though this simulated body may be completely different from your own, she feels as though she's holding onto your very soul.
That's an order. You're coming with me.
You shake your head and start to answer, but the shriek of an incoming shell cuts you off.
You both react instantly and throw yourselves aside.
A smoking crater is left where you were standing only moments earlier.
Adelyde pulls you to your feet and runs toward the boarding bridge.
Two Red soldiers are still waiting anxiously beside the bridge. The moment they see you coming, they rush forward to help.
But the pirates have already noticed the transfer between the two ships. Gunfire and shells begin raining toward the bridge.
A cannonball screams straight toward the crossing.
At the last possible moment, before stepping onto the bridge, you release Adelyde's hand.
The shell destroys the boarding bridge completely. The sea opens between the two ships once more.
Adelyde grips the railing and stares at you in disbelief.
You still had enough strength, and your reflexes were more than fast enough. Don't try to tell me you couldn't make it.
Because I never intended to obey that order.
We're equals. You don't have the authority to order me.
I'm still the commandant of this fleet. Until the danger has passed, I stay here to the end.
I'm leaving my people with you.
You turn and begin walking toward the bridge entrance on the far side of the deck.
Then you remember one final thing and turn back toward the commander you have come to respect.
The old alliance salute is still clear in your memory, but you want to set aside everything artificial about the simulation and offer her a proper F.O.S. salute.

You thank her for believing in you, for honoring the history and bond once shared by both sides, and for respecting your choice. The old salute is for her—and for the peace these factions might still achieve, even if all of this is only a simulation.
You smile at her through a face that isn't truly yours.
You find yourself wondering whether her face is also a system-generated mask as the ships slowly drift farther apart.
